rv.cn: Jane Edwardes, Maxie Szalwinska and Thomas W Hodgkinson
rv.q: Death of a Salesman Piccadilly, London W1 ★★★★★ Arthur Miller’s 1949 play was written for a big Broadway theatre, which perhaps explains why the Young Vic’s revival is even more powerful here than it was back home. Heading a great cast, Wendell Pierce is magnificent as the stubborn salesman who can’t tell the difference between dreams and reality.
Marianne Elliott and Miranda Cromwell’s meticulous production holds you mesmerised for over three hours, and the ending is devastating.
Despite its often-dreamy pace, these carefully observed moments mean that ‘Death of a Salesman’ has a real urgency to it.
This brilliant but testing production is a fierce, powerful example.
This is a good production — originally at the Young Vic and now transferred to the West End — to see if you have reservations about the torrent of words in Arthur Miller's most famous play.
People will be talking about it for years to come.

Marianne Elliot and Miranda Cromwell’s extraordinary revival of Arthur Miller’s classic mints the play fresh, it looks as if it was written today, for our times, and is one of the most moving experiences I’ve had in the theatre this year.
It's emotionally draining but entirely worth it.
Her magnificent performance lends a note of hope to the ultimate tale of modern sorrow.

cn.t: Critics overwhelmingly praise this revival of Miller's classic, with Wendell Pierce and Sharon D Clarke delivering powerhouse performances. A rare theatrical triumph.
